title: Giant rogue waves were doubted until a sensor caught one in 1995
body: For centuries sailors described walls of water appearing out of nowhere, and many scientists doubted them, because standard wave models said such giants should be almost impossibly rare. On 1 January 1995, instruments on the Draupner gas platform in the North Sea recorded a wave 25.6 m high, while the waves around it were about 12 m. It was the first rogue wave ever measured by an instrument, and it pushed oceanographers to rethink how waves combine.
